Without memory access, I'm going in blind—but here are some genuinely excellent sci-fi books:

**Classics that hold up:**
- *Dune* (Frank Herbert) — dense but rewarding, political intrigue + desert ecology
- *The Left Hand of Darkness* (Ursula K. Le Guin) — beautiful, anthropological sci-fi
- *Neuromancer* (William Gibson) — cyberpunk origin, short and punchy

**Modern standouts:**
- *Project Hail Mary* (Andy Weir) — optimistic problem-solving in space, *The Martian* energy
- *A Memory Called Empire* (Arkady Martine) — diplomat in an alien empire, gorgeous prose
- *The Expanse* series (James S.A. Corey) — hard sci-fi, politics, mystery

**Weirder/speculative:**
- *Anathem* (Neal Stephenson) — philosophy monks in a clockwork world, not for everyone but I loved it
- *Children of Time* (Adrian Tchaikovsky) — evolution as narrative, very different

What kind of vibe are you after? Space opera, near-future tech, philosophical, action-heavy?
Time travel—great pick. Here are some solid ones:

**Mind-bendy & clever:**
- *Dark Matter* (Blake Crouch) — multiverse, not strictly time travel but same energy, compulsively readable
- *Recursion* (Blake Crouch) — false memories, time loops, tight pacing
- *The Gone World* (Tom Sweterlitsch) — time-traveling FBI agent investigating an apocalyptic murder, dark and twisty

**Classic & influential:**
- *The Time Traveler's Wife* (Audrey Niffenegger) — emotional, romance-forward, time as tragedy
- *Slaughterhouse-Five* (Kurt Vonnegut) — fragmented, anti-war, "so it goes"
- *The End of Eternity* (Isaac Asimov) — mechanics-focused, time police keeping history "on track"

**Heavier / more literary:**
- *Kindred* (Octavia Butler) — Black woman pulled back to antebellum South, brutal and necessary
- *The Ministry of Time* (Kaliane Bradley) — recently out, time refugees adjusting to modern London, witty but has teeth
- *This Is How You Lose the Time War* (Amal El-Mohtar & Max Gladstone) — epistolary, two enemy agents falling in love across timelines, very poetic

**If you want something lighter/fun:**
- *How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe* (Charles Yu) — meta, funny, sad under the hood

Any of those sound like your speed?
